noticias.titulo: Potential AI slowdown is not ‘end of the world’ for data center real estate, says Digital Realty CEO - CNBC
noticias.resumo: While cloud, storage, enterprise IT and internet services all require data center capacity, artificial intelligence has quickly become the dominant driver of demand.  AI could account for about 70% of global data center capacity demand by 2030, according to a report from McKinsey.  The report said the capital outlay needed to meet total data center demand by 2030 will be nearly $7 trillion.

noticias.resumo:
# Stocks Slide as AI and Oil Jitters Hit Sentiment: Markets Wrap

Equities fell around the world after leaders of the biggest artificial-intelligence firms proposed slowing the technology’s development, while a jump in oil prices sapped risk sentiment further. 

Tech stocks led declines as traders fretted that efforts to rein in the advance of cutting-edge AI could dent the boom driving hundreds of billions of dollars in capital expenditure.  Nasdaq 100 futures sank 1.

noticias.titulo: Wall Street weighs prospect of an AI slowdown on data center buildout - CNBC
noticias.resumo:
That chatter ramped up on Monday, as AI infrastructure stocks sold off following a proposal over the weekend from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to slow the pace of frontier model development. 

Amodei wrote that a slowdown in AI development doesn't mean "halting model training or technical progress. "

Still, GE Vernova's stock dropped almost 9% on Monday, as Caterpillar sank more than 4%, Vertiv fell close to 8% and Oracle slipped almost 4%.

noticias.titulo: Santoli: The youthful phase of AI is over. What it means for investors - CNBC
noticias.resumo: There are positives here.  If a year ago the most-cited concern was that an AI bubble was forming and speculative exuberance was frothing over, that's been taken care of.  The savage purge since June of high-momentum stocks – dominated by AI hardware and related industrials – has sapped the bullish aggression of traders, helping to reset tactical sentiment toward a more neutral level.
